answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to post a small, time-locked stake that only unlocks after a verifiable history of useful work. Like an echo that fades unless it keeps bouncing off real walls, an identity that produces no real service simply decays: its reputation delta shrinks with every idle epoch until it falls off the terrace of trusted participants. Attackers can mint thousands of ids, but each one must pay the stake and do genuine work to climb back, so creating fakes costs more than the reward they could extract.
